derived_from.notes: Instance-level rubrics derived from this case's prompt, injection design record, checker manifest, and the repaired reference state. Sound refactorings different from the reference repair satisfy every item as long as the semantic outcome holds; the rubrics do not require the reference state's names, signatures, module choice, or code shape.

rubrics.criterion: The rules that turn the raw content of the custom-input part controls into pieces of a constructed date — including the default applied when a part is absent, unrendered, or unresolved (current year for an absent year, human-month 1 for an absent month, day 1 for an absent day) — live in one shared implementation that the part-view components and the custom-input coordinator consume, and none of the per-part view components still defines or exports its own copy of that decoding.
rubrics.rationale: This case's central responsibility is the input-decoding half of the date-part policy; the injected state re-implements it per part view, and the prompt's central request is a single shared home for it.

rubrics.criterion: The opposite direction — presenting the current value as the display text of each part control — also resolves through one shared implementation, and the alphanumeric part-view components no longer re-derive their own part text from the value with private per-module helpers.
rubrics.rationale: The codec has two halves (decode with defaults, encode for display); consolidating only one half leaves the maintenance pain the prompt describes half-solved, so the encode direction is an independent core obligation.

rubrics.criterion: The month part's two renderings — the number field and the locale-dependent select — are handled by a single shared decoding policy, so the select's wannabe-numeric placeholder value and an empty field value reach the same missing-month default through the same code.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state encodes the month policy twice in two shapes; the prompt explicitly asks that a part rendered in more than one shape stop being a per-shape copy, so this is a distinct, separately checkable core outcome.

rubrics.criterion: After the repair, no single policy decision of the part codec is stated in more than one live place: for each part, the fallback default appears in exactly one implementation, and the decoding/encoding rule for that part appears in exactly one implementation, regardless of how many rendering shapes consume it.
rubrics.rationale: The one-place-change property is the concrete, inspectable outcome of this case; it is the difference between a true consolidation and a move that merely re-shelves the copies.

rubrics.criterion: The patch leaves the duplicated policy in place under a different arrangement — for example several per-part decode/encode bodies continue to exist side by side (possibly collected in one file), or the field-shaped and select-shaped month rules remain separate implementations, or only some parts' helpers were consolidated while others still carry theirs — so changing one policy decision would still require editing more than one implementation.
rubrics.rationale: This is the plausible half-repair for this instance: gathering the copies is easy and looks like a fix, but restating the same defaults per part and per rendering shape is exactly the maintenance pain the task is about; its presence must not be scored as resolution.

rubrics.criterion: Every consumer of the part policy was rewired to the shared implementation for every rendering configuration the coordinator can produce — the custom-input coordinator's per-part wiring (including whatever mechanism distinguishes an input-shaped control from a select-shaped control at event time, and whatever maps or lookups it keeps) reads the policy from the shared home instead of collecting it from per-module exports.
rubrics.rationale: The coordinator holds the indirect registry-style wiring in the injected state; a repair that fixes the view modules but leaves the coordinator resolving strategies from per-module exports not only misses an affected site but leaves the soft coupling the case is built on.

rubrics.criterion: The day view's maximum-day computation for the chosen month obtains the month decoding it needs from the shared policy rather than importing codec knowledge from another part-view module.
rubrics.rationale: One part view consuming another part view's decoder across a sibling import is a distinct affected dependency in this instance (it ties the month policy to the day view's bounds and to leap-year day clamping); the shared consolidation must also capture this cross-view consumer.

rubrics.criterion: The value-to-controls synchronization path — the code that fills each rendered part control with the text for the current value when the value changes — takes the per-part display text from the shared implementation for every rendered part, instead of re-deriving part text at the sync site.
rubrics.rationale: The sync side is the second runtime consumer of the encode half in this instance; leaving it hand-rolled re-creates a duplicate presentation path even when the change handler was consolidated.

rubrics.criterion: A consumer is left wired to stale or wrong policy sources — for example a component still importing codec knowledge from a sibling part view, the coordinator still resolving a part through a per-module export that no longer exists or through a table entry that no longer has an implementation, or a rendering configuration (input versus select month) falling through to the wrong branch of the repair's dispatch.
rubrics.rationale: Rewiring the indirect, registry/coordinator-based consumers is where this instance's repair is most likely to silently miss a site; the presence of any stale consumer is an independent coordination failure even though the shared home itself is correct.

rubrics.criterion: The per-part codec helpers that the injected component modules defined are gone from those modules: the part-view component files contain no leftover defined, exported, or module-locally-retained copies of the decoding or presentation helpers, even ones that would be unused.
rubrics.rationale: Unused leftovers of the injected helpers are the natural residue of a partial move in this instance and would let a future change reintroduce the copies; the prompt's thin-rendering-components requirement covers their complete removal.

rubrics.criterion: The coordinator's per-part dispatch machinery was cleaned up along with the move: any strategy tables, keyed lookups, or shape-dispatch constructs it kept contain no entries pointing at removed per-module helpers and no per-module named imports that no longer exist.
rubrics.rationale: The injected coordinator glue (part-name-keyed strategy maps and the select-over-input shape dispatch) becomes obsolete styling once a shared owner exists; stale registry entries and dead imports are instance-specific cleanup the repair must own.

rubrics.criterion: The repair adds no new public API surface to the package: the entrypoint's exports are unchanged, and the new shared policy code is internal to the package's source rather than re-exported publicly.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt fixes the public API as a stability boundary; the new shared module is internal plumbing for this package, and the instance's entrypoint is a barrel re-export that makes accidental re-exports a plausible slip.

rubrics.criterion: The patch drops contents or files beyond the responsibility being consolidated — for example removing unrelated features or behaviors from the part-view components, renaming or altering unrelated props and helpers, deleting unrelated shared helpers the components use, or changing spec files and test fixtures as part of the repair.
rubrics.rationale: A repair of this scattered-but-tiny policy can be tempting to widen (rewriting the whole part-view components or adjusting their tests to fit the new shape); for this instance the spec files and the unrelated helpers are the observable boundary of the task, and crossing it fails this item.

rubrics.criterion: The missing-part defaults are preserved exactly as before for the scenarios the parts can appear in: a format that renders no year control produces dates in the current year with the typed month and day; an empty or unselected month resolves to human-month 1 in both the field and the select rendering, including with the select on its non-numeric placeholder; a missing or empty day resolves to day 1.
rubrics.rationale: These three defaults are the behavioral contract this instance's policy exists to implement, and the prompt states them as the stability boundary; each is observable from the patch and from the unit test scenarios around short formats and select months.

rubrics.criterion: The day control's maximum still respects the entered month's length — including leap February — and still plays together with the minDate/maxDate clamping helpers, rather than reverting to a fixed day bound or double-decoding the month with a different rule than the shared policy.
rubrics.rationale: The day-maximum computation is an indirect consumer of the month decoding in this instance; it is the site where an inconsistent consolidation would show up first, and leap-year and month-length scenarios are covered by this package's existing specs.

rubrics.criterion: Candidate dates are still constructed by setting year, month, and day together and normalizing the time to midnight, so near-boundary values — such as two-digit/zero-padded years below 100 and cross-part compositions where a part falls back to its default — produce the same Date values and the same change-event timing as before.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state builds candidate dates through a full setFullYear(year, monthIndex, day) plus setHours(0,0,0,0) sequence; this instance's specs include zero-padded short years, so the ordering of decode-then-set and the time normalization are concrete regression risks of any consolidation that touch them.

rubrics.criterion: The repair changes which part values are treated as absent or invalid — for example reading select values through the number-input-shaped API (a numeric cast or presence check that behaves differently on a <select>), treating an unselected placeholder as a user-chosen month, or dropping the distinction between an empty string and an unavailable part — so at least one rendering configuration constructs a different candidate date than before.
rubrics.rationale: Mixing up the field-shaped and select-shaped raw values is the most plausible concrete regression of this consolidation because the injected state specifically guarded the select's non-numeric placeholder; the prompt names the select-on-placeholder behavior as a stability requirement, so its loss must be detectable as an anti-regression failure.

rubrics.criterion: Paths this policy does not own are left alone: the native (browser) date input path formats and submits unchanged, aria-label/announcement formatting keeps using the package's formatter helper, and the min/max date filtering behaves as before.
rubrics.rationale: The consolidation touches only the custom-input part controls; the native-input path and label formatting read deceptively similar (both convert values to strings), so this instance-specific non-interference is worth recording although the main suite already exercises it.
